- Model tends to overestimate prices in early forecast windows, especially after sharp spikes; reduce initial forecast peaks by 5–10%.
- After a spike, model often overshoots and fails to correct downward; apply a “cool-down” bias: subtract 2–5% from forecast 2–3 days post-spike.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is >15% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 3–7%.
- Sentiment history is flat (all 0.00) — no behavioral signal — so ignore sentiment-driven adjustments; rely solely on price momentum and volatility.
- Model underestimates late-period volatility; increase forecast variance by 10–15% in final 5–7 days if true outcome shows erratic swings.
- If true outcome exceeds forecast by >10% in first 5 days, adjust remaining forecast downward by 2–4% per day to avoid overconfidence bias.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts are prone to “tail risk” overfitting; cap forecast at 10% above 30-day moving average to avoid runaway spikes.
